5:
\textbf{(a)} $x=(1+\cos\theta)\cos\theta$, $y=(1+\cos\theta)\sin\theta$.
\[\frac{dx}{d\theta}=-\sin\theta\cos\theta-(1+\cos\theta)\sin\theta=-\sin\theta(1+2\cos\theta),\qquad\frac{dy}{d\theta}=\cos\theta+\cos2\theta.\]
$\frac{dx}{d\theta}=0$ when $\sin\theta=0$ or $\cos\theta=-\frac12$: $\theta=0,\pi,\frac{2\pi}3,\frac{4\pi}3$. At $\theta=\pi$ also $\frac{dy}{d\theta}=0$ (the cusp at the origin, not a vertical tangent). Vertical tangents at \boxed{\theta=0,\ \tfrac{2\pi}{3},\ \tfrac{4\pi}{3}}.

\textbf{(b)}
\[A=\frac12\int_0^\pi(1+\cos\theta)^2d\theta=\frac12\int_0^\pi\Big(\frac32+2\cos\theta+\frac{\cos2\theta}{2}\Big)d\theta=\boxed{\frac{3\pi}{4}}.\]
\textbf{(c)} $V=\iint_Ry\,dA=\int_0^{\pi/2}\int_1^{1+\cos\theta}r\sin\theta\,r\,dr\,d\theta=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{(1+\cos\theta)^3-1}{3}\sin\theta\,d\theta$. With $u=\cos\theta$:
\[V=\frac13\int_0^1\big((1+u)^3-1\big)du=\frac13\Big[\frac{(1+u)^4}{4}-u\Big]_0^1=\boxed{\frac{11}{12}}.\]
6:
$(-\pi,0)$ corresponds to $t=\pi$. $x'=\cos t-t\sin t$, $y'=\sin t+t\cos t$, $x''=-2\sin t-t\cos t$, $y''=2\cos t-t\sin t$. At $t=\pi$: $x'=-1$, $y'=-\pi$, $x''=\pi$, $y''=-2$.
\[\kappa=\frac{|x'y''-y'x''|}{(x'^2+y'^2)^{3/2}}=\frac{2+\pi^2}{(1+\pi^2)^{3/2}},\qquad R=\frac1\kappa=\boxed{\frac{(1+\pi^2)^{3/2}}{2+\pi^2}}\approx3.02.\]

Reverse the order: $0\le x\le2$, $0\le y\le4-x^2$ is the same as $0\le y\le4$, $0\le x\le\sqrt{4-y}$:
\[\int_0^4\frac{e^{2y}}{4-y}\int_0^{\sqrt{4-y}}x\,dx\,dy=\int_0^4\frac{e^{2y}}{4-y}\cdot\frac{4-y}{2}dy=\frac12\int_0^4e^{2y}dy=\boxed{\frac{e^8-1}{4}}.\]
9:
Maximize $P=xy^2z^3$ with $x+y+z=100$. Using $\ln P=\ln x+2\ln y+3\ln z$ and Lagrange: $\frac1x=\frac2y=\frac3z=\lambda$, so $y=2x$, $z=3x$ and $6x=100$:
\[\boxed{x=\tfrac{50}{3},\quad y=\tfrac{100}{3},\quad z=50}.\]
